summary: Turn the signed Connector SDK plugin security plan into a host-owned dry-run/test sandbox with production-credential isolation, mediated DNS-pinned egress and executable resource-limit evidence without opening provider admission.

impacts.evidence: Dry-run/test sessions are host-created per connector/account binding; production credential tiers are forbidden in non-production test mode and no global tenant credential authority is introduced.
Dry-run results store only bounded identifiers, change digests, route templates, usage and isolation evidence; full provider payloads, query strings and secret values are excluded.
Two additive Draft 2020-12 sandbox contracts are introduced; existing Connector SDK and Task-025 contracts are unchanged.
Task 029 adds no EventBus event type and changes no existing event payload.
Task-025 AdmissionPlan grants and limits now have a host-owned executable dry-run/test interpretation while Connector SDK v1 root interfaces remain unchanged.
Task 029 adds no persistent table or database migration.

Production credentials fail before broker access, dry-run suppresses all credential/network providers, test egress is exact-grant DNS checked and IP pinned, and Linux namespace/chroot isolation is externally probed.
Task 029 deliberately provides no production-credential override; any future exceptional override requires a separate explicit approval design rather than a sandbox flag.
Result records carry connector/version/request/capability identity, resource-change hashes and normalized isolation evidence suitable for later audit attachment without credential content.
Sandbox preview does not change Inbox/Outbox/reconciliation algorithms; dry-run is side-effect free and test behavior remains connector capability scoped.
Host egress planning re-resolves exact granted DNS destinations, rejects private/special addresses and pins the approved IP plus TLS server name so provider code cannot perform a second DNS lookup.
Signed wall/CPU/RSS/output/concurrency ceilings now produce measured usage and fail-closed limit outcomes in the Linux reference runner.
No migration exists; rollback removes the sandbox runtime while provider admission remains disabled. Temporary chroot roots are removed after every reference execution.

Unit tests cover credential isolation, side-effect-free dry-run, exact egress, DNS rebinding, special-address rejection and output limits; a Linux external process probe verifies environment/filesystem/network isolation.
